answers:
Vaccines are a safer way for your body to learn to make antibodies. COVID-19 vaccines work by training your body's natural immune system to recognize and fight the virus that causes COVID-19. When the vaccine is introduced to your body, it stimulates a response to the virus, causing your body to make antibodies that help kill or neutralize the virus. If you're exposed to the actual virus in the future, these antibodies will help your immune system recognize and fight the virus quickly, preventing serious illness.
The vaccines teaches your cells how to make a protein that triggers an immune response. Once your cells have finished using the instructions, they break down the mRNA and get rid of it.
You can learn more about how COVID-19 vaccines work on the CDC website.

The current COVID-19 vaccines, and the vaccines still in development, use one of these methods:

An inactivated virus
A harmless piece of the virus
A gene from the virus

None of these can cause COVID-19.
Learn more about how COVID-19 vaccines work on the CDC website

 Vaccines protect you, your family, and your community

COVID-19 Vaccines And Testing | VA Montana Health Care | Veterans Affairs
Veterans who decide to get a COVID-19 booster vaccine outside of VA are encouraged to share this information with your VA health care team.  

You can send a picture of your CDC COVID-19 Vaccination Record Card to your VA provider through secure messaging. 
Or, bring your vaccine card with your next appointment so staff can enter that into your health record.  
You can also add your vaccine information to your MyHealtheVet health summary for your own records. To add your information, you’ll need a premium MyHealtheVet account.
